 Cameron Johnson had an efficient 23 points (9-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, a steal and four 3-pointers in win over the Grizzlies.
 Cameron Johnson has been much better in his second season’s with the Nuggets than he did last year. His ability to be a threat off of Jokic is something defenses have to respect. He won’t score 23 points and fill up the box score every night, but the Grizzlies struggled to defend him and he’ll have games like this every once in a while. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cameron Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokić will start Monday’s game against the Rockets. 
 All five Nuggets’ starters were upgraded from questionable to probable on Monday afternoon, and they’re now available. The Nuggets will roll out their usual starting five against the Rockets. 
 DeMar DeRozan 
 DEN 
 Guard-Forward 
 #10 
 DeMar DeRozan (back) and Cameron Johnson (lower body) have been upgraded to probable for Monday’s matchup with the Rockets. 
 DeRozan and Denver’s starting five have all been upgraded to probable, and the six are expected to take the court after returning home from Saturday’s win over the Pacers in Mexico City. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson (lower body) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Johnson, who has missed time this season with an ankle injury, played 29 minutes in Saturday’s win over the Pacers. If he can’t play on Monday, the Nuggets may turn to Bryce Hopkins to fill the resulting void in the starting lineup. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson accumulated 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), four rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Pacers. 
 Making his fifth appearance of the season, Johnson’s effort on Saturday was the best of the bunch. He shot 66.7 percent from the field, and his 18 points were a season high. Johnson has hit double figures in three of the four games he’s played since returning from an ankle injury that sidelined him for three games last month. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson (lower body) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Raptors. 
 There was some concern that Johnson may have injured his hamstring during Monday’s game against the Trail Blazers. However, he’s feeling better and will take his usual place in the starting lineup on Wednesday. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson (lower body) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Raptors. 
 Johnson appeared to tweak something in his left leg during Monday’s loss to the Trail Blazers, ending his night with just over one minute remaining. The good news is that he’s probable to play on Wednesday. If Johnson can’t play, Trevon Brazile could move into the starting five. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson finished with seven points (2-of-5 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals and one three-pointer against the Trail Blazers on Monday. 
 Johnson checked out of this game with 1:08 remaining after appearing to tweak something in his left leg. Head coach David Adelman didn’t have an update after the game, so there isn’t any conclusion to draw at this point, other than Johnson could be hurt and miss time. If that happens, Trevon Brazile or Alpha Diallo will likely step into a starting role in place of Johnson.

 Diallo has missed Denver’s last four games with a sprained wrist. If he can play on Monday, the rookie wing will come off the bench, as Cameron Johnson returned from a sprained ankle on Friday against the Suns.

 Zach Edey scored two points (1-of-4 FGs), five rebounds, and a block in 19 minutes on Wednesday. 
 Largely, Edey has been disappointing this year. His numbers are down from his rookie year and the minutes are a career low. His FG% is down 11.4% from last season. His value with size is important to this team, but the Grizzlies have good backup centers with Isaiah Stewart and Quinten Post who can take minutes from him. It’s getting harder to hold in redraft leagues with the ups and downs.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Sandro Mamukelashvili accounted for 23 points (9-of-15 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.
 Mamukelashvili was at his best during the second quarter, shooting 4-of-4 from the field and scoring 10 points. He didn’t provide much beyond points and three-pointers, but Mamu has been productive enough this season to merit a roster spot in deep leagues.
